# Automata Framework — Full Documentation for LLMs

> Automata is a deterministic 2D game framework for the modern web and Ruken platform.
> Strict Core Laws: Koota ECS determinism, Effect outside sim, Zero Eval CSP, PixiJS 2D sub-tick alpha interpolation.

---

# The 5 Golden Rules for LLMs
1. Simulation is Pure and Deterministic: NEVER import Effect, browser DOM, or PixiJS inside simulation systems.
2. Effect Outside the Sim: Side effects (I/O, audio, network, saves) run in Effect outside the sim.
3. Zero Eval: Never use eval() or new Function(). Strict CSP compliance required.
4. Sub-tick alpha interpolation: Presentation interpolates positions between ticks: prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha.
5. Single State Ownership: Only the sim mutates game entities; UI and presentation only observe truth.

---

## Document: Overview & Vision (Getting Started)
URL: /docs/overview
Description: High-level architecture, design laws, and Ruken-first direction.

# AutomataFramework: overview

> **Owner direction, 2026-10-11:** AF is **Ruken first**. Core packages are built from proven code in FloorFifty (2D), The Last Light (the PixiJS 3D experiment) and Ruken itself; everything else is a modular extension. PixiJS renders 2D and 3D. Effect runs everything outside the sim; the sim stays on Koota. CI/CD, deployment, mobile UI and the content compiler come first, in M1. AF is finished on 2D (FloorFifty) and 2.5D (The Last Light); a 3D game is then built on AF and its 3D pieces are merged back. This replaces the 2026-10-05 direction (all A/B specs first, a future 3D game, then "Part C" extraction).

## Read order and document ownership

1. This overview.
2. The [Ruken-first master spec](superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-automata-framework-ruken-first-design.md) and its [extraction map](superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-core-and-extensions-extraction-map.md). The [2026-10-01 master spec](superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-automata-framework-overview-design.md) still owns the laws, state ownership and determinism rules that the new spec does not replace.
3. [01 Decomposition](01-decomposition.md): packages, milestones, dependencies and the old-phase mapping.
4. [02 Master delivery plan](02-master-delivery-plan.md): the only task list, with task IDs.
5. [03 Continuation](03-continuation-prompt.md): current status, blockers and the exact next action.
6. [04 How we build](04-how-we-build.md): how a task flows from spec to merged PR.
7. The milestone's spec, the ADRs (`docs/adr/`), the spike verdicts (`docs/spikes/`) and the task's plan when one exists.

The numbering and roles match Ruken's own `docs/00`–`04`. Dated specs own architecture and behavior; the numbered documents own navigation, order and status. `AGENTS.md` holds the working rules and `CLAUDE.md` imports it.

## Purpose

AutomataFramework makes Ruken games mostly content and game logic. Versioned `@mcthaydt/automata-*` packages provide a deterministic Koota simulation, a content compiler, an Effect-based runtime, a Ruken-first host layer, PixiJS rendering, mobile-first Svelte UI, testing harnesses and the CI/CD and packaging that put a game on Ruken (and on a standalone site) with no per-game plumbing.

The seven laws stand: only the sim changes gameplay state; the server owns networked truth; each state has one owner; presentation observes truth; the sim has no I/O or wall clock; identical seed, content and ordered inputs reproduce; the host is a port, and Ruken is the reference host.

## Decisions in force

| Decision | Record |
|---|---|
| Koota ECS behind the sim facade | [ADR 0001](adr/0001-ecs-choice.md) |
| PixiJS for 2D (core) and 3D (`render-pixi3d` extension on `@pixi/3d`) | [ADR 0002](adr/0002-pixi-for-2d-and-3d.md) |
| Effect for runtime, host, tooling and pipelines; never inside the sim; Zod stays the schema language | [ADR 0003](adr/0003-effect-outside-the-sim.md) |
| Ruken first: consume `@ruken/sdk`, `@ruken/sdk-host`, `@ruken/manifest` and `ruken publish` (which validates); follow Ruken's doc and milestone process | [ADR 0004](adr/0004-ruken-first-host.md) |

Decisions D-1 to D-6 (the `@pixi/3d` beta dependency, adoption scope, lint tooling, standalone hosting, GPU runner, vendored Ruken packages) run on their recommended defaults since 2026-10-11 until the Owner overrides them; see the master spec §12. M1 runs in parallel lanes ([04 How we build](04-how-we-build.md#lanes-2026-10-11)).

## Product and engineering priorities

- **One look.** Endesga 64 palette, Bubble Bobble mixed with Celeste, in 2D, 2.5D and 3D ([art direction](art/README.md), Owner 2026-10-11).

- **Ship to Ruken early.** M1 ends with a blank game built, validated by Ruken's own checks, published to Ruken and playable on a phone. Everything after builds on a working pipeline.
- **Mobile first.** Layout is designed and tested at phone sizes first, with FloorFifty's geometry, target-size and reachability rules. UI tests do not need a renderer, server or full journey.
- **Core is small and proven; extensions are opt-in.** A capability is core only if Ruken requires it of every game or both reference games need it.
- **Fast feedback with honest gates.** Focused runs for iteration; full parity, GPU, release and device gates remain separate and required.
- **Evidence controls status.** Drafted, reviewed, implemented, locally verified, CI verified, deployed and Owner accepted are different facts.

## Current checkpoint

M0 (spikes S1–S6, ADR 0001, the A1a sim core) is merged. Nothing from M1 onward is implemented. M1 runs in parallel lanes, each writing its own task spec against the [M1 shared contracts](superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-m1-shared-contracts-design.md); the Owner review of the Ruken-first restructure (M1.0a) is pending. See [03 Continuation](03-continuation-prompt.md).

## Scope map

| Milestone | Scope |
|---|---|
| M0 Foundation | Spikes, ECS decision, sim core (done) |
| M1 Blank game on Ruken | Toolchain, Effect runtime skeleton, content compiler, host, boot and loading, 2D renderer, mobile UI primitives, CI/CD, packaging, publish, dev host, example, minimal `create-game` |
| M2 Deterministic core complete | Physics, goldens and replays, publishing |
| M3 2.5D and pipelines | `render-pixi3d` at 2.5D scope, `post-retro`, the pipeline platform, 2.5D character and props pipelines |
| M4 Input and display complete | All input paths and display policy, E2E matrix |
| M5 Saves, audio, localization | Ruken saves and migrations, audio extensions, six languages |
| M6 Gameplay extensions | Sectors, nav, puzzle, systems, narrative, cutscenes, feel, debug, environment pipeline |
| M7 Online and store | `net`/`server`, `store`, `host-tauri` |
| M8 CLI 1.0 and adoption | Full CLI, 1.0 (AF finished for 2D and 2.5D), a slice of FloorFifty and The Last Light running on AF |
| GAME-3D | A 3D game built on AF 1.0, in its own repo |
| M9 3D merge | The 3D game's proven pieces merged back into AF |
| M10 Website (final phase) | The AF site: store, documentation, playable demos and everything else a framework site needs |

**Business model (Owner, 2026-10-11, recorded only):** Tailwind-style. The core is free; extensions are paid, sold individually or through an all-access pass on the site. Extensions therefore stay separate packages with no core file edited by any of them, so paid ones can move to a private repo and registry later. Licensing and distribution are decided at M10.0 (D-7).

External inputs (Ruken package publication and F1, GitHub Packages tokens, runner capacity, hosting accounts) are tracked in [01 Decomposition](01-decomposition.md) §6; do not infer readiness from a planned date.

## Document: Quick Start (Getting Started)
URL: /docs/quick-start
Description: Scaffold your first Automata game in seconds with npx automata.

# Quick Start Guide

Start building deterministic browser games in seconds using the official CLI.

## Installation

```bash
# Create a new Automata 2D game project
npx automata create-game my-game

# Enter project directory
cd my-game

# Install dependencies and start development server
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

## Project Anatomy

A standard Automata game project has three clean layers:

```
my-game/
├── src/
│   ├── sim/             # Pure deterministic ECS logic (Koota)
│   │   ├── traits.ts    # Entity components & schemas
│   │   └── systems.ts   # Movement, combat, collisions
│   ├── render/          # PixiJS visual representation
│   │   └── views.ts     # Sprites, shaders, animations
│   └── main.ts          # Effect runtime bootloader & loop
└── package.json
```

> [!TIP]
> The `sim/` folder never imports browser APIs, PixiJS, or Effect. This guarantees your game logic can run headless on a multiplayer game server or inside a test runner.

---

## Document: ECS Simulation & Determinism (Core Simulation)
URL: /docs/sim-ecs
Description: Fixed 60Hz timestep, Koota ECS traits, and bit-identical replays.

# ECS Simulation & Determinism

The heart of Automata is a pure, deterministic simulation built on Koota ECS.

## Fixed Timestep Simulation Loop

The simulation advances in discrete, uniform steps of exactly 16.666ms (60 ticks per second):

```typescript
import { createSim, defineTrait } from '@mcthaydt/automata-sim'

// Define traits as pure schemas
export const Position = defineTrait({ x: 0, y: 0 })
export const Velocity = defineTrait({ vx: 0, vy: 0 })

// Create sim instance
export const sim = createSim({
  fixedDeltaMs: 16.666,
  systems: [
    (world) => {
      // Query entities with Position and Velocity
      world.query(Position, Velocity).each(([pos, vel]) => {
        pos.x += vel.vx
        pos.y += vel.vy
      })
    }
  ]
})
```

## Deterministic Verification

Every commit runs cross-engine replay testing across Chromium (V8), WebKit (JavaScriptCore), and Firefox (SpiderMonkey). A 500-tick run produces bit-identical XXH64 state hashes.

---

## Document: PixiJS 2D Presentation (Rendering)
URL: /docs/render-pixi
Description: Sub-tick alpha interpolation, entity views, and WebGL2/WebGPU shaders.

# PixiJS 2D Presentation Boundary

Automata enforces a strict boundary between simulation state and visual rendering.

## Sub-Tick Alpha Interpolation

High refresh-rate monitors (120Hz, 144Hz, 240Hz) render faster than the 60Hz simulation. To avoid jitter, Automata calculates sub-tick alpha:

```
alpha = accumulator / fixedDeltaMs
position_rendered = prev_pos * (1 - alpha) + current_pos * alpha
```

```typescript
import { createPixiRenderer, type EntityView } from '@mcthaydt/automata-render-pixi'

const playerView: EntityView = {
  container: playerSprite,
  update(curr, prev, alpha = 1) {
    const p = prev?.transform ?? curr?.transform
    const c = curr?.transform
    if (c && p) {
      playerSprite.x = p.x + (c.x - p.x) * alpha
      playerSprite.y = p.y + (c.y - p.y) * alpha
    }
  }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> PixiJS v8 automatically uses WebGPU when supported by the client device, falling back seamlessly to WebGL2.

---

## Document: Effect Runtime & Concurrency (Architecture)
URL: /docs/effect-runtime
Description: Structured concurrency, typed errors, and automatic resource scoping.

# Effect Runtime & Concurrency

Outside the simulation loop, everything is managed by Effect.

## Typed Error Boundaries

Rather than uncaught runtime exceptions crashing the game canvas, all failures are typed and handled:

```typescript
import { Effect, Scope } from 'effect'
import { bootGame, type BootError } from '@mcthaydt/automata-runtime'

const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const scope = yield* Scope.make()
  const runtime = yield* bootGame({
    canvasId: '#game',
    manifestUrl: '/assets/manifest.json'
  })
  return runtime
}).pipe(
  Effect.catchTags({
    AssetLoadFailed: (err) => Effect.logError('Assets failed', err),
    WebGLContextLost: (err) => Effect.logWarning('Restoring context', err)
  })
)
```

## Resource Scoping

Textures, audio streams, and event listeners are automatically cleaned up when game rooms exit, eliminating memory leaks.

---

## Document: Zero-Eval CSP & Ruken Security (Security)
URL: /docs/security-csp
Description: Running games under strict Content Security Policy without eval or new Function.

# Zero-Eval CSP & Ruken Security

Games on the Ruken platform execute inside an isolated iframe with a zero-trust Content Security Policy:

```http
script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
```

> [!WARNING]
> Most game engines rely on `new Function` or `eval` to compile shaders, schemas, or accessor expressions. Under Ruken, this throws an immediate `EvalError` and terminates execution.

## The Automata Solution

- **No-Eval Shader Programs:** Shaders are linked statically via `@mcthaydt/automata-render-pixi/no-eval`.
- **Precompiled Accessors:** Koota ECS accessors use array structs without dynamic code generation.
- **Zod Ahead-Of-Time Validation:** Schemas validate without JIT code generation.

---

## Document: Mobile UI Primitives (UI Primitives)
URL: /docs/mobile-ui
Description: Responsive geometry ownership, safe areas, and touch controls.

# Mobile UI Primitives

Automata UI is mobile-first, designed for phones, tablets, and handheld devices.

## Geometry Ownership & Reachability

The geometry owner handles viewport scaling, virtual safe areas, and touch zones:

```typescript
import { createGeometryOwner } from '@mcthaydt/automata-ui'

const geometry = createGeometryOwner({
  window,
  root: document.documentElement,
  referenceWidth: 320,
  referenceHeight: 192
})
```

## Virtual Controls

Touch joysticks and virtual buttons respond to multitouch without interfering with browser gestures.

## Document: AI Coding Agent Rules (AI & Skills)
URL: /docs/ai-rules
Description: Official rules, constraints, and guardrails for AI coding assistants.

# AI Coding Agent Rules & Guidelines

When generating code for Automata Framework games, AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Antigravity) MUST obey the 5 Golden Rules.

## The 5 Golden Rules for LLMs

1. **Simulation is Pure and Deterministic:**
   - NEVER import `effect`, browser DOM, `window`, `document`, or PixiJS inside `packages/sim` or game simulation files.
   - Simulation logic must run synchronously and deterministically.
2. **Effect Outside the Sim:**
   - Side effects (file saving, networking, audio, timer intervals) belong strictly in the runtime layer using Effect.
3. **Zero Eval:**
   - NEVER generate `eval()`, `new Function()`, or dynamic code evaluation. It violates Ruken's strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`).
4. **Sub-Tick Alpha Interpolation:**
   - Entity views must interpolate positions between previous and current ticks:
   ```typescript
   x_render = prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha
   ```
5. **Single State Ownership:**
   - Only simulation systems mutate entity components. Presentation only observes `RenderDelta`.
